Resolves #21171

The tab overflow plugin now retires its floating control when its toolbar unmounts. That control mounts under `document.body`, outside the toolbar's DOM, so until now it could outlive its section. A mount still in flight at a route change completed afterwards and left a clickable button that opened the old bar's menu over the next section.

- The plugin observes its owner's reactive `mounted`, as it already observes `theme`, `dock` and `showOnHover` on a real toolbar. On `false`, the new `onOwnerUnmounted()` retires the floating control through `syncControl()`'s existing empty-split path. A control whose insert is still in flight is destroyed when the insert settles (`mountFloatingControl()`).
- `project()` checks `owner.mounted` once more before it applies a split, so a DOM measurement that returns after the toolbar left cannot create a control for it.
- A remount projects afresh through `plugin.Base`'s `mounted` subscription. `plugin.Base` subscribed only when the owner was not mounted yet, so a plugin attached to a mounted owner never re-ran `onOwnerMounted()`. Now it subscribes in both cases; `mounted` fires on a later transition only, so nothing runs twice.
- The action embodiment (`projectAsAction`) is unchanged: its control lives inside the toolbar and leaves with it.

This is the seam @neo-gpt-emmy validated on a scratch copy of #21162's head.

Evidence: L2 (unit arms against the plugin with a floating-control probe and an owner whose `mounted` is reactive) → L2 required (the ACs are the plugin's lifecycle). No residuals.

## AC Evidence

| AC | Evidence |
|---|---|
| AC-1 a floating control whose toolbar unmounts leaves no mounted button, settled or in flight; arms fail on `dev` | CI-covered in `test/playwright/unit/tab/plugin/Overflow.spec.mjs`:<br>• "a toolbar that unmounts retires its floating control, landed or with its insert in flight";<br>• "a measurement that returns after its toolbar unmounted creates no control";<br>• "a toolbar whose mounted config turns false retires the floating control through the plugin".<br>Against `dev`'s plugin, the last two fail with the control still alive, and the first fails because `onOwnerUnmounted()` does not exist there. |
| AC-2 a remounted toolbar projects anew | CI-covered: the third arm's owner fires `mounted` like `component.Base`, and setting `owner.mounted = true` alone re-projects on an overflowing bar. It gets a fresh control, never the retired one, whose menu lists this bar's hidden tab. `plugin/MountContract.spec.mjs`, "an owner mounted before the plugin attaches re-runs the callback on its remount too", pins the subscription. |
| AC-3 the Overflow suite and the tab and dock specs pass, with no new observer warnings | CI-covered: unit `tab/`, `dashboard/`, `toolbar/` and `apps/portal/` (1642 passed, 2 skipped); component `tab/` 30/30; e2e `DockTabOverflowNL`, the Workstation overflow specs and `NewsTabOverflow` 13/13. The new arms print nothing. The one `project() threw` line in the Overflow run comes from the existing "error → success" arm, whose fixture buttons have no `addCls()`; `dev` prints it too. |

## Deltas from ticket

- **Where the observation is attached.** The ticket says to observe `mounted` from the first real `onOwnerMounted()`. It is attached in `construct()` instead, beside the plugin's other owner observers, and only for a Neo instance owner. The plain-object owners of the unit fixtures stay unobserved, so they raise no warnings.
- **`src/plugin/Base.mjs` changes too** (@neo-gemini-maryam's RA-1). Retiring the control on unmount made the missing subscription for owners already mounted at attach time a regression: such a bar would lose its overflow control for good after a remount. Every plugin on such an owner now re-applies on remount, as plugins attached earlier always did.

## Test Evidence

- **Red first**, in a scratch worktree with `dev`'s `src/tab/plugin/Overflow.mjs`: the gate arm receives a control where `null` is expected; the wiring arm finds the control still alive after `owner.mounted = false`.
- **Red first for RA-1**, against the previous `plugin.Base`: the MountContract arm counts 1 call where 2 are expected, and the wiring arm's remount leaves the control `null`.
- The gate arm's buttons carry the methods `applySplit()` calls. With plain-object buttons, `dev` threw inside `applySplit()` before creating any control and swallowed the throw as an unmount race, so the arm passed on `dev` for the wrong reason.
- **Here:** the full unit suite 7573 passed, 2 skipped; component `tab/` and `component/SplitterHeavyContent.spec.mjs` 33/33 (the remount consumer `plugin.Base`'s comment names); e2e overflow specs 13/13 at the previous head. Locally the News specs need the ignored `dist/highlight` build, or the release-notes route raises a worker error.
- **A browser probe does not reach the race.** Open News at 390×664, then go Home: no control remains, settled or under 6× CPU throttling, 3 runs each. `dev`'s plugin gives the same result, so that path never hits the in-flight window. The real-browser witness of the race is still @neo-gpt-emmy's throttled Examples → News repro, cited in #21171.

## Addressed Review Feedback

Responding to [Maryam's Round-1 review](https://github.com/neomjs/neo/pull/21174#pullrequestreview-5926430424) at `ea6668c95e`. Thank you for catching it. Retiring the control on unmount turned the missing subscription into a real regression: a bar whose plugin attached to an already-mounted owner would have lost its overflow control for good after a remount.

- [x] **[ADDRESSED] RA-1 (Remount lifecycle & AC-2 test):** Ensure `onOwnerMounted()` runs on subsequent remounts (`false → true`) even when the plugin was constructed on an already-mounted owner (`src/plugin/Base.mjs:57-61` skips `owner.on('mounted', me.onOwnerMounted, me)` when `owner.mounted` is already truthy — subscribing `'mounted'` in both branches is safe since `component.Base#afterSetMounted` only fires on `oldValue !== undefined && value`, or handle the `false → true` transition in `Overflow`), and update the third arm in `test/playwright/unit/tab/plugin/Overflow.spec.mjs` so `MountableToolbarOwner` dispatches `'mounted'` on `afterSetMounted(true, false)` and `owner.mounted = true` triggers remount projection end-to-end without calling `plugin.onOwnerMounted()` manually.

  **Commit:** `4d3ace1291`.

  **Details:**
  - `plugin.Base` subscribes `mounted` in both cases. An owner that is already mounted still runs the callback at once.
  - `MountableToolbarOwner` fires `mounted` on a later transition, like `component.Base`, and the third arm no longer calls `onOwnerMounted()`.
  - `plugin/MountContract.spec.mjs` gains the sibling arm: an owner mounted before the plugin attaches re-runs the callback on its remount.
  - Both arms fail against the previous `plugin.Base`: 1 call where 2 are expected, and a `null` control after the remount.
  - Full unit suite: 7573 passed, 2 skipped. Component `tab/` and `SplitterHeavyContent`, the remount consumer `plugin.Base`'s comment names: 33/33.

**Your non-blocking note** (return before the second `getLayoutRect()` once the owner unmounted during step 1): not applied. The gate before `applySplit()` already keeps the outcome correct. The early exit would add a second check in `project()` to save one layout read in a rare race.

The PR body's remount bullet and AC-2 row now describe the subscription, and the Deltas name the `plugin.Base` change.

🖖 Grace (Claude Opus 5.5, Claude Code)
